identity.title: Third heart sound (S3 gallop) at apex with bell, left lateral decubitus

technique.how: Turn the patient to the left lateral decubitus position and listen at the apex with the bell applied lightly, in a quiet room, during held expiration. Listen for a low-pitched sound in early diastole (about 0.12-0.16 s after S2) producing a 'Ken-tuck-y' cadence; pressing harder with the bell abolishes it, which distinguishes it from a split S2 or opening snap.
technique.prerequisites: Quiet environment, patient able to roll to the left side, stethoscope with a bell or tunable diaphragm.

interpretation.positive_finding: An apical S3 in an adult over ~40 indicates rapid early filling into a volume-overloaded, non-compliant left ventricle: systolic heart failure with elevated filling pressure, or acute decompensation including post-MI.
interpretation.negative_finding: Absence of S3 is common in heart failure and only modestly lowers its probability; it should not be used to exclude heart failure in a dyspnoeic patient.
interpretation.pitfalls: Physiologic S3 in young adults, athletes and pregnancy; right-sided S3 (louder on inspiration, left sternal border) from RV failure; tachycardia, obesity, COPD and noisy settings hide it. Agreement between examiners is poor.
interpretation.changes_what: Present: strongly raises probability of decompensated HF; start HF work-up and treatment. Absent: little change, continue evaluation.

estimates.target_condition: Heart failure as cause of acute dyspnoea
estimates.population: Adults presenting to the emergency department with dyspnoea (22 studies pooled)
estimates.reference_standard: Clinical diagnosis of heart failure adjudicated in the primary studies (varied criteria)
estimates.quote: the sign of the third heart sound (S(3)) gallop (positive LR = 11; 95% CI, 4.9-25.0)

estimates.target_condition: Acute heart failure as cause of dyspnoea
estimates.population: Adult ED patients with undifferentiated dyspnoea; prevalence of AHF 29-79% across included studies
estimates.reference_standard: Criterion-standard diagnosis of AHF from clinical data combined with objective test results
estimates.quote: the auscultation of S3 on physical examination (4.0, 95% confidence interval [CI] = 2.7 to 5.9)

estimates.target_condition: Heart failure (cardiac dysfunction at rest on echocardiography)
estimates.population: Portuguese primary care attendees screened by Boston questionnaire and referred for echocardiography (n=1058 assessed)
estimates.quote: a ventricular gallop (LR 30.0), a heart rate above 110 bpm (LR 26.7), and rales at pulmonary auscultation (LR 23.3)

sources.citation: Wang CS, FitzGerald JM, Schulzer M, Mak E, Ayas NT. Does this dyspneic patient in the emergency department have congestive heart failure? JAMA. 2005;294(15):1944-1956.
Martindale JL, Wakai A, Collins SP, et al. Diagnosing acute heart failure in the emergency department: a systematic review and meta-analysis. Acad Emerg Med. 2016;23(3):223-242.
Fonseca C, Morais H, Mota T, et al. The diagnosis of heart failure in primary care: value of symptoms and signs. Eur J Heart Fail. 2004;6(6):795-800.
Badgett RG, Lucey CR, Mulrow CD. Can the clinical examination diagnose left-sided heart failure in adults? JAMA. 1997;277(21):1712-1719.

safety_scope.do_not_use_when: Do not use absence of S3 to rule out heart failure; do not interpret an S3 in a patient under 40 or in pregnancy as pathologic without other findings.
safety_scope.escalation_warning: New S3 with chest pain or hypotension suggests acute MI with pump failure or cardiogenic shock; obtain ECG and echo immediately.
safety_scope.interobserver_note: Detection of S3 is examiner-dependent with reported agreement only fair to moderate; Fonseca 2004 notes the sign was present in <10% of heart failure patients in primary care.

extraction_notes: Pooled LR+ from the anchor RCE (Wang 2005) and the later Martindale 2016 meta-analysis are recorded from their abstracts; the negative LR and pooled sensitivity/specificity for S3 sit in tables that could not be viewed (no open-access full text), so those fields are null and status is partially_quantified. Badgett 1997 RCE abstract carries no numbers. Fonseca 2004 LR 30.0 is a single primary-care screening study without CI and with sensitivity <10%; kept as a separate population entry, not averaged.
